chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about the foundling (lqa'it), he said: 'It is not sold and it is not bought.'

key_terms.اللَّقِيطِ: Foundling; a child whose parents are unknown and is found abandoned.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a foundling child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam clarifies the status of the *lqa'it* (foundling) by prohibiting their sale or purchase, thereby distinguishing them from chattel slaves while affirming their right to freedom. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that a foundling retains their inherent human dignity and is not subject to commercial transaction, ensuring their care and eventual emancipation are managed as a public trust rather than a private asset.
